cues.en: This seems wrong. I think most people believe you turn a bike simply by pointing the handlebars in the direction you wanna go. After all, this is how you drive a car. Point the front wheels any direction you like, and the car just goes that way.
cues.zh: 这看起来不太对。我觉得大多数人都以为，骑车只要把车把转向想去的方向就行了。毕竟，开车就是这样。前轮想往哪边打，车就往哪边开。

cues.en: But the difference with a bicycle is steering doesn't just affect the direction you're headed, it also affects your balance.
cues.zh: 但自行车和汽车不同，转向不仅会影响行进方向，也会影响你的平衡。

cues.en: Imagine you wanna make a right turn, so you steer the handlebars to the right.
cues.zh: 想象一下，你想右转，于是把车把往右打。

cues.en: What you've done is effectively steered the bike out from under you. So now you're leaning to the left,
cues.zh: 实际上，你是把自行车从身下转开了。现在你就会向左倾斜，

cues.en: and the ground puts a force on the bike to the left, so the only way not to fall is to steer the bike to the left.
cues.zh: 地面也会给自行车一个向左的力，所以要想不摔倒，你只能把车往左转。

cues.en: You have made a left turn.
cues.zh: 结果你转了个左弯。

cues.en: If you really wanted to turn right, you first have to counter steer to the left, so you can lean right into the turn.
cues.zh: 如果真想右转，你得先向左反打方向，这样才能向右倾斜进入弯道。

cues.en: This is something anyone who rides a bike knows intuitively,

If I'm balancing it and I just start walking toward you, it will always fall away from you. If I want to walk toward you, it's easy enough to do and people inherently know how to do it. If I pull it backward, I can now start walking
cues.zh: 这很直观。骑自行车就跟我们说的“倒立摆”一模一样，或者说像用手掌立扫帚。如果我立着它并直接朝你走去，它肯定会往反方向倒。如果我想走向你，其实很容易，大家天生就知道怎么做。如果我先把它往后拉，现在就能开始往前走——

cues.zh: 往那边走了。我必须先引发倾斜，对，顺势转过去。如果你想把倒立摆移到某个位置，得先反方向移动底座。

cues.en: And now the pendulum is leaning in the direction you wanna go so you can move with it.
cues.zh: 这时倒立摆就倒向你想去的方向，你就可以跟着它走了。

cues.en: And it's the same with a unicycle.
cues.zh: 独轮车也是同样的道理。

cues.zh: 为了往前走，你得先往后蹬一点，这样身体就会前倾，

cues.en: the turn. Right. I mean, the wild takeaway is that steering is not just for turning the bike. Steering is for balancing. That's exactly right. Why is it hard to balance on a stationary bike?
cues.zh: 转弯。对。我的意思是，最让人意外的结论是，操控方向不只是为了让自行车转弯，也是为了保持平衡。没错。为什么在静止的自行车上很难保持平衡？

cues.en: I think most people believe it's because the wheels aren't spinning, so there's no gyroscopic effect.
cues.zh: 我觉得大多数人认为，这是因为车轮没转，所以没有陀螺效应。

cues.en: But that's not it.
cues.zh: 但并不是这样。

cues.en: The truth is you use steering to keep the bike underneath you, but steering doesn't work when you're stationary.
cues.zh: 事实是，你靠转动车把让自行车保持在身下，但静止时转动车把不起作用。

cues.en: Your balance comes not so much from how you position your body over the bike, but by how you steer the bike to keep it underneath you.
cues.zh: 保持平衡并不主要靠调整身体在车上的位置，而是靠转动车把，让自行车保持在身下。

cues.en: Even when going straight, you're constantly making small steering adjustments to maintain balance. You're moving the contact patch of the front wheel under you. You're doing exactly what you do when you balance a broomstick on your hand.
cues.zh: 即使直线骑行，你也一直在微调车把来保持平衡。你在把前轮的接地点移到身下，做的正是用手掌平衡扫帚时的动作。

cues.en: And so if the rider is responsible for steering the bike to keep it balanced, how do bikes without riders stay upright?
cues.zh: 那么，如果骑手要靠转动车把来保持自行车平衡，没有骑手的自行车又是怎么保持直立的？

cues.en: As long as a bike is moving with sufficient speed, it can keep coasting indefinitely.
cues.zh: 只要自行车有足够的速度，就能一直滑行下去。

cues.en: I first became aware of this phenomenon through the great videos by MinutePhysics,
cues.zh: 我最早是通过 MinutePhysics 的精彩视频了解到这一现象的，

cues.en: which inspired me to make this video. You should definitely check them out.
cues.zh: 这些视频启发我制作了这期视频。你一定要去看看。

cues.en: But it turned out the ground where we went to test this effect was really bumpy.
cues.zh: 但后来发现，我们去测试这一现象的地面非常颠簸。

cues.en: But the bike still manages to absorb all these perturbations
cues.zh: 可自行车还是能吸收这些扰动，

cues.en: and remain stable.
cues.zh: 并保持稳定。

cues.en: So how does it do this? I think most people believe it's the wheels spinning that creates some sort of gyroscopic effect that resists falling over.
cues.zh: 那它是怎么做到的呢？我觉得大多数人认为，是车轮旋转产生了某种陀螺效应，从而防止翻倒。

cues.en: Just like in this demonstration of gyroscopic precession, the wheel stays upright even though gravity is pulling it down.
cues.zh: 就像这个陀螺进动的演示一样，即使重力把它往下拉，车轮也能保持直立。

cues.zh: 但这并不是自行车稳定的原因。

cues.zh: 一秒钟都不安全。在转向锁死的自行车上保持平衡，和在静止的自行车上保持平衡一样难。不行。

cues.en: The real reason bicycles are stable without riders is because they're cleverly designed to steer themselves.
cues.zh: 自行车在没人骑的时候能保持稳定，真正的原因是它们被巧妙地设计成能自行转向。

cues.en: If they start falling to one side, the handlebars turn in that direction to steer the wheels back underneath them.
cues.zh: 如果它们开始往一侧倒，车把就会朝那个方向转，把车轮转回身体下方。

cues.en: At least three mechanisms are responsible for a bike's corrective steering.
cues.zh: 自行车能自动修正转向，至少有三个机制在起作用。

cues.en: The first is that due to the angle of the front fork, the steering axis intersects the ground in front of where the wheel touches the ground.
cues.zh: 第一个是：由于前叉的角度，转向轴与地面的交点位于车轮触地点的前方。

cues.en: So if the bike starts leaning to the left, the force from the ground on the tire turns the wheel to the left. If the bike starts leaning right, the force from the ground pushes the wheel to the right. The front wheel of a bicycle is essentially a caster wheel, like those you find on strollers or shopping carts. Whichever way you drive them, the wheel falls in line and rolls in the same direction.
cues.zh: 所以，自行车开始向左倾时，地面对轮胎的力会让车轮向左转；开始向右倾时，地面对轮胎的力会让车轮向右转。自行车前轮本质上就是一个脚轮，就像婴儿车或购物车上的那种。无论你往哪个方向推，轮子都会对齐并朝同一方向滚动。

cues.en: The second reason for a bike's corrective steering is that the center of mass of the handlebars and front wheel are located slightly in front of the steering axis.
cues.zh: 第二个原因是，车把和前轮的重心略微位于转向轴前方。

cues.en: So when the bike leans left, their weight pushes the front wheel to the left. If the bike leans right, their weight steers to the right.
cues.zh: 因此，自行车向左倾时，它们的重量会把前轮向左推；向右倾时，重量会让前轮向右转。

cues.en: And the third mechanism is a gyroscopic effect, but it doesn't keep the bike upright directly.
cues.zh: 第三个机制是陀螺效应，但它并不直接让自行车保持直立。

cues.en: It just helps steer.
cues.zh: 它只是帮助转向。

cues.en: If you have a gyroscope and you push down on the left hand side, the gyro will turn left.
cues.zh: 如果你有一个陀螺仪，并向下压它的左侧，陀螺仪就会向左转。

cues.en: If you push down on the right side, it will turn right.
cues.zh: 如果向下压右侧，它就会向右转。

cues.en: This is known as gyroscopic precession.
cues.zh: 这被称为陀螺进动。

cues.en: It seems as though the force you apply takes effect 90 degrees from where you applied it.
cues.zh: 看起来，你施加的力似乎会在与施力点相差 90 度的位置产生效果。

cues.en: So bikes are stable primarily because of steering.
cues.zh: 自行车之所以稳定，主要靠的是转向。

cues.en: They have built in mechanisms for steering themselves.
cues.zh: 它们内置了自我转向的机制。

cues.en: In fact, you don't need all three mechanisms to create a stable bike. Researchers created this weird looking bicycle to prove a point. It has no gyroscopic effect, thanks to counter rotating wheels above the wheels that touch the floor.
cues.zh: 事实上，你并不需要全部三种机制来造出一辆稳定的自行车。研究人员造了这辆造型古怪的自行车来证明这一点。它没有陀螺效应，因为接触地面的车轮上方装有反向旋转的车轮。

cues.en: Plus, there is no caster effect because the front wheel touches the floor in front of the steering axis.
cues.zh: 此外，它也没有脚轮效应，因为前轮接触地面的位置在转向轴的前方。

cues.en: But this bike is made stable by its mass distribution,
cues.zh: 但这辆自行车靠其质量分布保持稳定，

cues.en: the force of gravity on which steers it in the direction of any lean.
cues.zh: 重力的作用会把它转向任何倾斜的方向。

cues.en: Understanding how bicycles work is still an active area of research.
cues.zh: 理解自行车的运作原理至今仍是一个活跃的研究领域。

cues.en: There is a program you can use to input all the different bicycle parameters and see the range of speeds over which it is self stable.
cues.zh: 有一个程序，你可以输入各种自行车参数，查看它在哪些速度范围内能自我稳定。

cues.en: And this research is leading to better bikes. This prototype has a smart motor in the handlebars to actively help steer, keeping the bike upright even at low speeds.
cues.zh: 这项研究正在带来更好的自行车。这个原型车把里装了一个智能电机，主动辅助转向，即使在低速下也能让自行车保持直立。

cues.en: I guess it's fitting that we're still learning new things about bicycles
cues.zh: 我觉得挺合适的，我们仍在不断了解自行车的新知识，

cues.en: since most of us are able to ride one without any knowledge of how we're actually doing it.
cues.zh: 因为我们大多数人会骑自行车，却根本不知道自己到底是怎么骑的。
